regime_context: The detector shows a dispersed, non-one-narrative market: only 22 of 49 themes are trend-eligible (narrowing breadth), and the headline energy complex is challenged by low-momentum rotational churn. The one validated leg — the absolute-trend gate — helps on this market's history (gate_helps=true), so eligibility is a real risk filter, but nearly every eligible theme is crowded, which argues for size-down caution, not directional conviction. Track record direction accuracy is weak (0.444), so leans should default low.

theses.subject: US Energy Complex
theses.thesis: Energy is the only eligible theme combining strong momentum score (1.415), high durability (0.69), near-complete breadth (0.955) and trend-eligible status, so it is the prevailing leadership candidate in an otherwise fragmented tape. The cross-sectional rank is not alpha, but this is a case for continuity of the confirmed leader rather than a new call; the crowding flag (z=1.03) is a size-down caution, not a fade, per the guardrails.
theses.dissent: Crowded leadership at z=1.03 with hurst_tag='mixed' can stall; energy has no rank-IC edge and unscheduled macro share is 1.0, so headline-driven energy jolts can reverse without trend continuation.

falsifier.text: XLE lags SPY by 5% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Big Pharma
theses.thesis: Big Pharma is trend-eligible with the highest durability among top eligible names (0.79) and strong breadth (0.889), suggesting the absolute-trend gate is admitting a durable, broad uptrend. Despite crowded (z=1.68), the trend-gate is the one validated risk-control leg, so an eligible, high-durability, broad theme is a reasonable low-conviction overweight on staying power.
theses.dissent: Crowding is extreme (z=1.68, highest in top cohort), which historically marks attention spikes near tops and argues for reducing, not adding, exposure.

falsifier.text: PPH lags SPY by 5% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Health Care (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: Trend-eligible with high durability (0.74) and solid breadth (0.75), while being less crowded than Big Pharma (z=1.44). The equal-weight tilt diversifies single-name pharma risk within the same healthcare leadership, supported by the validated abs-trend gate.
theses.dissent: XLV proxy overlaps heavily with Big Pharma, so this is not an independent call; if healthcare leadership stalls, both fail together.

falsifier.text: XLV lags SPY by 5% before the check-by date
